text.p: Bonds closed down as Europe retreated, with some players taking the opportunity offered by remarks by Bundesbank chief Hans Tietmeyer to take profit.
Tietmeyer warned that the debt-to-GDP ratio was also a criterion for entry to the single currency and it was not simply a matter of budget deficits.

But the Portuguese market kept in step with Germany and Spain with prices remaining in a fairly narrow range. Nervousness over the single currency could be felt again on Friday when the market will also be awaiting producer price data from the United States.

The shorter end may be affected by June inflation figures to be released in Spain on Friday, although gains could be limited even if the numbers are good as the market is anxious to see the numbers for Portugal which will be issued on Monday.
The escudo closed calm at 100.97/00 to the mark in a market devoid of volatility.
Traders see the rate remaining in a range of 100.80-101.10 on Friday providing the dollar stays above 1.75 marks.
